settings.heading: A living Christian civilization
settings.subheading: Heirloom goods drawn from the beauty of Rome, Byzantium, and Christian Europe — refined and dedicated to the glory of God.

settings.caption: A Roman temple become a church

settings.heading: Made to be kept
settings.text: Nothing mass-produced. Everything carved, cast, woven, or bound to last.

settings.heading: What endures
settings.text: Christ is King. His is the kingdom that outlasts every empire. We tell the old story of light and shadow to remember what endures — and to make things worthy of it.

settings.heading: A communion of saints and heroes
settings.text: Carved in marble and cast in bronze — the faithful, the valiant, and the wise who carried the light across the ages.

settings.name: Christ the King
settings.text: The kingdom that outlasts every empire — the center of all we make.

settings.name: Saint Michael
settings.latin: Quis ut Deus? — Who is like God?
settings.text: Captain of the host of Heaven, defender against the ancient enemy.

settings.name: Our Lady
settings.text: The first disciple; her yes carried into the world.

settings.name: Saint George
settings.text: The soldier-saint who faced the dragon — courage for the innocent.

settings.name: Constantine
settings.latin: In hoc signo vinces — In this sign
settings.text: Who saw the Chi-Rho and turned an empire toward the faith.

settings.name: Julius Caesar
settings.latin: Alea iacta est — The die is cast
settings.text: The order and craft of Rome — the inheritance faith would later refine.

settings.title: On the Chi-Rho
settings.text: The ancient monogram of Christ, and why it guides us.

settings.title: Rome, made new
settings.text: How Christian craft transformed a classical world.

settings.heading: The Kingdom that endures
settings.text: Earthly empires rise and fall, but the Kingdom of Christ endures forever.
